text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Right-wing Popular Party (PP) leader Manuel Monteiro will negotiate with Prime Minister Antonio Guterres whether to approve the details of the 1997 budget.
- A pilot with Portuguese state airline TAP has been accused of smuggling nearly one kilo of diamonds into the country on a flight from Luanda this month.
- The Sonae group is in the process of choosing an insurer to sell insurance products at its retail bank which is expected to open soon in its shopping centres.
- The debts of Portugal's health service will reach 106.2 billion escudos at the end of 1997, according to data released by the health ministry yesterday.

- Mobile phone company Telecel will distribute 50 percent of its net profits in dividends in 1998, according to analysts of SBC Warburg, one of the global coordinators of the flotation next month of a 35.6 percent stake in the company's capital.
- Unions linked to the judicial police threaten a strike next month if Justice Minister Jose Vera Jardim does not adhere to their demands for danger money.
- Petrogal president Manuel Ferreira de Oliveira urged the government to protect the diesel refining industry.
- A plan presented by four leading industrialists to Prime Minister Antonio Guterres to protect the forest stock in Portugal will cost 600 billion escudos in the next decade.
- Portugal should have no problems in getting 1997 EU cohesion funds, the director of the fund Jean-Francois Verstrynge said in Lisbon yesterday.
